solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Journal almost preserves deadlock

indicators.note: almost the whole word: JAMS stops one letter short

blocks.note: a log is a daily record, a journal
preserves = JAMS, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper nearly keeps a stalemate going.
explanation.walkthrough: "Preserves" reads as a verb acting on "deadlock", but it is the noun: jams, as in jars of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a jam of floating logs, and so any deadlock where nothing can move.

clue.text: Bit of atmosphere in old region

blocks.note: O = old, a standard abbreviation
a zone is a region

explanation.surface: A touch of period atmosphere in some historic district.
explanation.walkthrough: "Atmosphere" suggests mood or ambience; here it is literal, the air around the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a gas forming a layer of the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Poke live circuit, making no sense at all

blocks.note: to jab is to poke
to be is to live, to exist
a ring is a circuit, a loop

explanation.surface: Prodding a live electrical circuit is a senseless thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: "Live circuit" reads as one electrical phrase; split it, and "live" is the verb BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Jabbering is talking rapidly and unintelligibly.

clue.text: Essential to warm up petulant fool

indicators.note: the answer is essential to, contained within, the words that follow

blocks.note: warM UP PETulant

explanation.surface: Advice that a sulky idiot needs warming up first.
explanation.walkthrough: MUPPET is British slang for a fool, from the puppets of The Muppet Show.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a muppet calls them a fool.

clue.text: Leave Flower of Scotland on TV

indicators.note: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B

blocks.note: a TV is a television set
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Forth is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: Leave the anthem Flower of Scotland playing on the television.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower of Scotland is Scotland's unofficial national anthem, which makes the surface convincing; here "flower" is a flow-er, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: setting forth on a journey means departing, the intransitive sense of leave.

clue.text: Son bartering upset Windy City

indicators.note: windy as in winding, twisting: the letters wind about

blocks.note: S = son, as in family trees
anagram fodder, 14 letters

explanation.surface: A boy's trading has gone wrong in Chicago.
explanation.walkthrough: "Windy City" is Chicago's nickname, and "upset" looks like the anagram indicator; in fact "upset" is fodder and "Windy" is the indicator, leaving plain "City".
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Petersburg is a city, Russia's second largest.

clue.text: Beg hotel to move play area

indicators.note: the letters are told to move into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: Pleading with a hotel to shift its children's play area.
explanation.walkthrough: "Play area" suggests a playground; the plays meant are Shakespeare's, staged at the Globe theatre in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Globe is a theatre, an area where plays are performed.

clue.text: Record of the past?

blocks.note: the surface pushes a written record, a chronicle; the setter means a gramophone record, a song
not history but a song from years ago that is still played

explanation.surface: A history book, or an archive document.
explanation.walkthrough: "Record of the past" suggests a chronicle; the record is a song on vinyl, one from years ago.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an old song or record that is still played.

clue.text: Will exam abruptly change time?

indicators.note: cut off abruptly, so AMEND loses its last letter

blocks.note: an exam is a test
change = AMEND, cut short
T = time

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an exam's timing will be moved at short notice.
explanation.walkthrough: "Will" opens the clue like an auxiliary verb asking a question; it is the noun, a last will and testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a will, the document disposing of a person's property after death.

clue.text: Bird reportedly noses around wooden spoon?

indicators.note: as it is reported, spoken: the sound of PRIES is wanted

blocks.note: the booby is a seabird
to pry is to nose around

explanation.surface: A bird is said to poke its beak around a wooden kitchen spoon.
explanation.walkthrough: A wooden spoon is the mock prize for coming last, a British tradition from Cambridge exams and rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby prize goes to whoever comes last, as the wooden spoon does.

clue.text: Piece of furniture from French king

blocks.note: des is French for from the (or of the), before a plural noun
K = king, as in chess

explanation.surface: An antique piece of furniture that belonged to a king of France.
explanation.walkthrough: "French king" reads as one person, Louis perhaps; split it, and "from French" is DES.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the desk is one kind of furniture, the one people write and work at.

clue.text: Always returning fee for letter, showing respect

indicators.note: going back, so EVER is read from the end

blocks.note: ever = always, as in for ever
a letter here is one who lets a property; rent is his fee

explanation.surface: A postage charge that keeps coming back, paid politely.
explanation.walkthrough: "Letter" is not mail but someone who lets out a flat or house, and what a letter charges is rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means feeling or showing deep respect.

clue.text: Bruce, perhaps, with custom rope?

blocks.note: Bruce Lee, the martial-arts film star; "perhaps" says he is one Lee of many
a way is a custom, a habit

explanation.surface: Bruce, maybe, using a made-to-order rope.
explanation.walkthrough: "Rope" means freedom of action, as in giving someone enough rope; the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room to manoeuvre, the slack or rope someone is allowed.

clue.text: Prepare to fly with one on duty

indicators.note: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B

blocks.note: a duty is a tax, as on imports
I = one, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Getting ready to take off with someone who is on shift.
explanation.walkthrough: "On duty" reads as working a shift; "duty" is a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft taxis along the ground to the runway before take-off.

clue.text: American opening up road vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, reversing the word

blocks.note: A = American
a pore is a tiny opening in the skin
a lane is a road

explanation.surface: A US citizen opening up a road.
explanation.walkthrough: "Opening up road" reads like building a new road; "up" belongs to "opening", turning PORE over.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: anything that carries people or goods is a vehicle, and aircraft count as well as cars.

clue.text: Retiring setter and chief editor given a raise?

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so ME is read backwards

blocks.note: the setter is the puzzle's author, who calls himself me
a boss is a chief
ED = editor

explanation.surface: A crossword setter about to retire, and his editor, get a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: "Given a raise" suggests a pay rise; the raise is a raised design, stamped up from the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Embossed paper or leather has a design raised on it.

clue.text: Maligns an awful line manager?

indicators.note: awful as in badly made, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Staff badmouthing a dreadful boss.
explanation.walkthrough: "Line manager" is office jargon for a boss; the line is a railway line, managed from the signal box.
explanation.definitionFit: A signalman controls the signals and points on a stretch of railway line.

clue.text: Unit is second in manliness

blocks.note: Mach is the unit of speed relative to sound
is, as it stands
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Claiming one element comes second in being a real man.
explanation.walkthrough: "In" looks like it puts one piece inside another; it only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the Spanish word for a swaggering, exaggerated masculinity, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Doctor with a prayer for driving event

blocks.note: DR = doctor
a, as it stands
grace is a prayer said before a meal

explanation.surface: A doctor saying a prayer before a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration's break misleads: the wordplay splits the letters at different points from the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag race is a sprint between two cars from a standing start.

clue.text: One all in black possibly contracted by hospital

blocks.note: to contract an illness is to get it
H = hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A patient dressed in black who caught something in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: "Contracted" might suggest a shortened word; it means caught, as with a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Goths favour black clothes, hair and make-up; "possibly" admits not all do.

clue.text: Red line brought up in vehicle rental

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up moves the L higher, towards the top

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
a let is a rental, as in a holiday let
L = line; it moves up from CARLET to just after the C

explanation.surface: A red line drawn across a car-hire agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: CAR + LET gives CARLET; bring the L up two places and it becomes CLARET.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is red Bordeaux wine, and so its deep red colour.

clue.text: Publicise band’s drinking place

indicators.note: one who drinks takes something in, so SASH takes in PL

blocks.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder
PL = place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Advertising a band's favourite pub.
explanation.walkthrough: "Band" suggests musicians and "drinking place" a pub; both are false, and "drinking" is the verb, taking in what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash a story is to publicise it prominently, across a front page.

clue.text: Bouquet from first-class team in Italy

blocks.note: A = first-class, as in A1
AS Roma is a Serie A football club

explanation.surface: Flowers presented by a top Italian football side.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bouquet" suggests flowers; here it is a wine's smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from wine tasting, where the smell rising from the glass is called its bouquet.

clue.text: Friend’s reversing coach in course

indicators.note: reversing turns ALLYS round to SYLLA

blocks.note: an ally is a friend; ally's, with the S
a coach is a bus

explanation.surface: A friend is backing a coach onto a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: "Coach" suggests a trainer; it is a bus, and "reversing" works on the friend, not on the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the outline of topics to be studied stands for the course of study itself.

clue.text: University learned standard operation

blocks.note: U = university
sage as an adjective: wise, learned

explanation.surface: A university discovered its usual operating procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: "Learned" reads as the past tense of learn; it is the adjective, pronounced learn-ed.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the standard way something is done.

clue.text: Thanks company for Mexican dish

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks
CO = company

explanation.surface: Gratitude to a firm for providing Mexican food.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a folded Mexican tortilla with a filling.

clue.text: Rat grabbing a bit of sleep and plenty of food

indicators.note: SQUEAL grabs A and REM, holding them inside

blocks.note: to rat on someone is to squeal, inform
a, as it stands
REM sleep, the rapid-eye-movement phase

explanation.surface: A rodent snatching a quick nap and lots to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: "Rat" reads as the animal; it is the verb, to betray, which gives SQUEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: square here means solid and fair, so a square meal is a filling one, plenty to eat.

clue.text: Manage instrument cases and the rest

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so GONG encloses ETAL

blocks.note: a gong is a percussion instrument
et al, Latin for and others

explanation.surface: Looking after the instrument cases and all the other kit.
explanation.walkthrough: "Instrument cases" reads as luggage for musicians; "cases" is the verb, as in encases.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: how are you getting along? asks how you are coping, and to cope is to manage.

clue.text: Kind offer

blocks.note: the adjective: gentle and caring, soft of heart
a formal bid to do work at a price, as submitted for a contract

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two meanings: tender as an adjective, then as a noun or verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender heart is a kind one; a tender is a formal offer, as for a contract.
